column2: A new face has come asking to join [Root.Society.GetName]: [new_recruit.GetTitledName]. Our ways are old and plain. No one sits among us who has not first fought before us. I should go and tell the [new_recruit.GetManWoman] what is expected.
The Gods want blood. Let us see whose.
Yes-yes, new claw-fodder. Let it fight-prove!
Time ta see if dis one's got any fight in 'im.
I'll put on my sternest face. The Wolf likes that.
I shall explain the customs of the order.
Another beardling. Let's see what their steel is worth.
I'll put on my most fearsome face. Ahem.
You will meet §Y[new_recruit.GetTitledFirstName]§! and explain the trial by combat.

[champion_character.GetTitledName] of [champion_character.Society.GetName] looks at me through the slits of a helm crusted with old blood. "You want to walk the road to glory, [Root.GetBoyGirl]? Then you will walk it over someone. The Gods do not want words. They want to see you fight." An armoured fist points at the ring of warriors behind. "One of mine. Now. Win, or bleed well enough that the Gods take notice."

[champion_character.GetTitledName] circles me, sniffing, tail lashing. "You want-wish to serve the Warlords? Hmm-hmm. Many want. Few live. You fight one of my clawpack, yes-yes? Fight-win and you are of [champion_character.Society.GetName]. Fight-lose and..." The Skaven chitters. "Then we feast tonight."

[champion_character.GetTitledName] of [champion_character.Society.GetName] yellz right in me face. "Oi! Ya wanna join da boyz? Den ya gotta pruv ya ain't a runt, [Root.GetBoyGirl]." Da big git folds 'is armz an' grins wiv all 'is teef. "Ya fight one of da ladz. Ya win, ya'z in. Ya lose... well, it'll be funny anyway."

[champion_character.GetTitledName] of [champion_character.Society.GetName] meets me in the cold of the yard, a wolfskin over [champion_character.GetHerHis] shoulders. "Ulric gives nothing to those who ask, [Root.GetBoyGirl]. He gives to those who take." [champion_character.GetSheHe] nods at the warriors around the fire. "You will fight one of ours. Stand, and the Wolf will know your name. Fall and get up again, and he still might."

[champion_character.GetTitledName] of [champion_character.Society.GetName] receives me in the order's hall, beneath the banners of old campaigns. "Courage is not proven by asking, [Root.GetLordLady]. Our custom is a passage of arms with a brother or sister of the order, before witnesses." [champion_character.GetSheHe] gestures to the lists outside. "Acquit yourself with honour and you will be welcome. Shame yourself, and no gate of ours will open to you again."

[champion_character.GetTitledName] of [champion_character.Society.GetName] strokes [champion_character.GetHerHis] beard and looks me up and down for a long while. "Words are cheap, [Root.GetFirstName]. Steel is not. The Guild does not take a warrior for a good name or a long beard. You will fight one of ours, and the elders will watch. And mind, if you run, it goes in the book."

[champion_character.GetTitledName] of [champion_character.Society.GetName] greets me with a curt nod. "Another recruit? To sit among us you must prove yourself, [Root.GetBoyGirl]," the [champion_character.GetManWoman] says gruffly, arms folded. "You will fight one of our own. Win, or at least do not disgrace yourself, and you are welcome."

[champion_character.GetTitledName] of [champion_character.Society.GetName] eyes me up and down, doubtful at first, and then [champion_character.GetHerHis] face changes. "Hold. Are you of the blood of [founder_target.GetTitledFirstName]?" I nod. "Then the old songs walk in here with you! The trial is the same for everyone, mind. But I will be watching you very closely."
Let the Gods watch, then.
Yes-yes! I fight-win, quick-quick!
I'll smash 'im up!
Then I will fight, and the Wolf may judge me.
I accept the passage of arms.
Bring them on. My axe is sharp.
I will gladly fight to prove myself.
You agree to duel whoever §Y[champion_character.Society.GetNameCap]§! chooses for you.
On second thought, I prefer my blood inside me.
Wait-wait! I am... busy. Important-busy.
Skah, ain't joinin' sum dum mob!
Perhaps the hearth is warmer than the yard.
I fear I must withdraw my request.
Another year, perhaps. When my beard is longer.
Actually, I would rather not bloody my knuckles.
You will not try to join §Y[champion_character.Society.GetNameCap]§!.

[new_recruit.GetTitledFirstName] did not flinch when I explained our custom. The [new_recruit.GetManWoman]'s eyes lit up at the thought of a fight. After asking around, [duel_target.GetTitledName] has offered to cross weapons with the newcomer.
[new_recruit.GetTitledFirstName] listened to me explain our custom, then shook [new_recruit.GetHerHis] head and walked off. "Bleed for a seat at your table? I think not."
Show [new_recruit.GetHerHim] how it's done, [duel_target.GetFirstName].
A sparring duel will take place between §Y[new_recruit.GetTitledName]§! and §Y[duel_target.GetTitledName]§!.
Why, that little... The coward!
None of us expected much, but [From.GetBestName] came through the initiation duel without a scratch. It will be worth watching what the [From.GetManWoman] makes of [From.GetHerselfHimself] among us.

[From.GetBestName] took some bruises and a cut or two, but held [From.GetHerHis] ground well. I was not the only one who was pleased. Time will tell whether our road suits the [From.GetAgeAdjective] [From.GetManWoman].

[From.GetBestName] was badly hurt by [combatant_2.GetTitledFirstName], and still got back on [From.GetHerHis] feet. I expected my [combatant_2.GetRootRelation] to land a blow or two, but I did not expect the [From.GetManWoman] to want to join us even more afterwards.
Just as [combatant_2.GetTitledName] was about to show [From.GetTitledName] what a sparring match looks like, the [From.GetAgeAdjective] [From.GetManWoman] dropped [From.GetHerHis] weapon and ran.
Now that is what we want to see!
Another member? Good.
Still standing? Then welcome.
What a waste of a morning!
§Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! will be invited to join §Y[Root.Society.GetName]§!.
§Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! will be §Rbanned§! from joining §Y[Root.Society.GetName]§! for 10 years.

To [Root.GetTitledName],

Not a drop of your own blood was spilled, and that is a rare thing. The Gods have seen it. Come and take your place among [From.Society.GetName], and know that from now on every battle is an offering, and every offering is watched.

[From.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledName],

You bled, and you did not kneel. Good. Blood is the first coin of the Gods, and you have paid it. Your place among [From.Society.GetName] is waiting. Bring your scars. There will be more.

[From.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledName],

Not one scratch! Very good, very cunning. Too cunning, maybe? I will watch you, yes-yes. Come, you are of [From.Society.GetName] now. Serve well. Serve ME well, most of all.

[From.GetTitledName], Warlord

To [Root.GetTitledName],

You bleed-bled but you did not run-flee. Strange-brave! Come, you are of [From.Society.GetName] now. Lick the wounds and sharpen the claws. There is much killing to do, yes-yes.

[From.GetTitledName], Warlord

Oi, [Root.GetFirstName]!

Dat woz a proper krumpin'! Not even a scratch on ya. Da boyz are well impressed (an' a bit narked). Ya'z one of [From.Society.GetName] now. Get in 'ere an' find a choppa.

[From.GetFirstName], da Boss

Oi, [Root.GetFirstName]!

Ya got bashed up good, but ya kept standin'. Dat's da Orky way. Ya'z one of [From.Society.GetName] now. Da scars make ya look 'arder anyway.

[From.GetFirstName], da Boss

To [Root.GetTitledName],

The yard saw no blood of yours today, and the old warriors are still talking about it. The Wolf favours the strong, and you have shown your strength. Come to the fire. Your place among [From.Society.GetName] is waiting.

In Ulric's name,
[From.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledName],

You took your wounds like a warrior and you stood up again. Ulric asks no more than that. Come to the fire, and let the brothers and sisters of [From.Society.GetName] drink to your scars.

In Ulric's name,
[From.GetTitledName]

To the valiant [Root.GetTitledName],

I am told you came through the passage of arms without a single scratch. That is the kind of [Root.GetWarriorRole] this order would be honoured to count among its own. You are hereby invited to take your vows with [From.Society.GetName].

With respect,
[From.GetTitledName]

To the brave [Root.GetTitledName],

You were wounded in the passage of arms, yet you held to the end and yielded to no one. Courage under pain is the first virtue of a knight. You are hereby invited to take your vows with [From.Society.GetName].

With respect,
[From.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledName],

The elders watched, and the elders were satisfied, which is not a thing I write often. Not a scratch on you. Your name is entered among [From.Society.GetName]. Do not make us strike it out.

[From.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledName],

You were hurt and you did not yield. A dwarf does not yield. The elders have entered your name among [From.Society.GetName]. Get those wounds seen to, and then get back to the drill yard.

[From.GetTitledName]

To the valiant [Root.GetTitledName],

I am told you did not take a single scratch during your initiation! That is the kind of [Root.GetWarriorRole] we would be honoured to have at our table. You are hereby invited to join our ranks.

[From.GetTitledName]

To the brave [Root.GetTitledName],

You were hurt during your initiation, but you stayed on your feet, and that is what we ask. You are hereby invited to join our ranks.

[From.GetTitledName]
Glory to the Gods.
Yes-yes! I am of the Warlords!
WAAAGH!
Ulric hears.
I shall take my vows with pride.
About time.
Finally.
§Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! also sends you a white wolf pelt from the lodge's own trophies.

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

You ran. The Gods saw it, and they laughed. Do not come to us again. If you do, you will be the offering.

[From.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

You flee-fled! Even a slave-rat fights when cornered. Go away-away. Come back and I will have you skinned, yes-yes.

[From.GetTitledName], Warlord

Oi, [Root.GetFirstName]!

Ya ran off like a grot wiv a squig on 'is bum. Da boyz ain't stopped laughin'. Don't come back or we'z gonna krump ya proper.

[From.GetFirstName], da Boss

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

A wolf does not run from a fight. You did. Do not seek our fire again for many winters, or you will find it colder than you think.

[From.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

You abandoned the passage of arms before witnesses. There is no place in [From.Society.GetName] for those who flee the field. Do not seek our gates for many years to come.

[From.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

You ran. It has been written down. Do not come back to the Guild until a long time has passed, and even then, expect the elders to remember.

[From.GetTitledName]

To the COWARD [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

Needless to say, we are unimpressed by your behaviour, and hope you do not seek us out again any time soon, lest this offence escalate.

[From.GetTitledName]
The Gods can laugh all they like.
Not-fair! Not-fair!
Dey'll be sorry!
I am as ashamed as you are.
I have dishonoured myself.
I'll not forget this either.
I am as disappointed as you are.
You will be unable to join §Y[martial_society_to_join.GetName]§! for 10 years.

My [recruiting_parent.GetRootRelation] is in a strange mood at dinner tonight, talking about the Gods and how they look on those who only watch. Then [recruiting_parent.GetSheHe] sets down the knife. "Enough, [Root.GetFirstName]. When will you take the trial of [recruiting_parent.Society.GetName]? I did not raise you to grow old and forgotten."

My [recruiting_parent.GetRootRelation] watches me eat with narrow eyes. "You are big-strong now, yes? Strong enough to fight for the Warlords? [recruiting_parent.Society.GetName] needs claws. Mine are many. Yours... we will see-see, yes? Unless you are afraid-scared."

My [recruiting_parent.GetRootRelation] bangs da table so 'ard da grub jumps. "Oi, [Root.GetFirstName]! Ya'z big enuff now. When ya gonna join [recruiting_parent.Society.GetName] an' do some proper fightin'? I ain't 'avin' no runt in da family!"

My [recruiting_parent.GetRootRelation] keeps glancing at my sword arm over dinner, and talking about the winter hunts of [recruiting_parent.GetHerHis] youth. At last [recruiting_parent.GetSheHe] says it plainly. "The Wolf is calling you, [Root.GetFirstName]. When will you stand in the yard and take the trial of [recruiting_parent.Society.GetName]?"

My [recruiting_parent.GetRootRelation] is making some less than subtle remarks over dinner, about my horsemanship and my skill at arms. "Honestly, [Root.GetFirstName]," [recruiting_parent.GetSheHe] says at last, "when are you going to seek your spurs with [recruiting_parent.Society.GetName]?"

My [recruiting_parent.GetRootRelation] puts down [recruiting_parent.GetHerHis] tankard and looks at me across the table. "My own father was in the Guild. I am in the Guild. When are you going to stop hiding behind your beard and take the trial of [recruiting_parent.Society.GetName]?"

My [recruiting_parent.GetRootRelation] is making some less than subtle remarks over dinner, about my swordsmanship and how interested I am in war. "Honestly, [Root.GetFirstName]... when are you going to join [recruiting_parent.Society.GetName]?"
I have only been waiting for you to ask.
§Y[champion_character.GetTitledFirstName]§! of [martial_society_to_join.GetName] will be told.
[recruiting_parent.GetFatherMotherCap], I will carve my own path.
Your [recruiting_parent.GetFatherMother] will be disappointed.
My [new_recruit.GetSonDaughter] breaks into a broad grin. "I thought you would never ask! I will go to [champion_character.GetTitledFirstName] at once, [Root.GetFatherMother]."

My [new_recruit.GetSonDaughter] breaks into a broad grin. "I thought you would never ask!" Then the grin fades a little. "Wait. You are the one I have to face, aren't you? You will go easy on me, [Root.GetFatherMother]?"

My [new_recruit.GetSonDaughter] rolls [new_recruit.GetHerHis] eyes. "I will carve my own path, [Root.GetFatherMother]. Please, let me." When I say nothing, [new_recruit.GetSheHe] goes on: "And [champion_character.GetSocietyRank] [champion_character.GetTitledFirstName] is a bore."

My [new_recruit.GetSonDaughter] rolls [new_recruit.GetHerHis] eyes. "I will carve my own path, [Root.GetFatherMother]. And I am not going to fight in a yard so you can judge me in front of your friends."
I was only waiting for you to be ready!
We'll do this properly. You're a recruit like any other!
§Y[new_recruit.GetTitledFirstName]§! will tell you how the trial went.
Why, you ungrateful little...!
§Y[new_recruit.GetTitledFirstName]§! is clearly not ready for this.

My [new_recruit.GetSonDaughter] comes to dinner tonight and cannot stop talking about the initiation duel. "It was wonderful, [Root.GetFatherMother]! And now I am one of [new_recruit.Society.GetName]!"
I knew you had it in you, [new_recruit.GetFirstName].
§Y[new_recruit.GetTitledFirstName]§! has joined §Y[new_recruit.Society.GetName]§!.
You almost make me wish I had never left...
You feel a little homesick for the old days.
Are you trying to impress me or something?
You scowl at the excited [new_recruit.GetManWoman].

My [new_recruit.GetSonDaughter] comes to dinner tonight and says nothing for what feels like an eternity. When I try to coax a word out of the [new_recruit.GetBoyGirl], [new_recruit.GetSheHe] mumbles, red with shame: "I am not like you, [Root.GetFatherMother]. I failed the trial."

My [new_recruit.GetSonDaughter] comes to dinner tonight and says nothing for what feels like an eternity. When I try to coax a word out of the [new_recruit.GetBoyGirl], [new_recruit.GetSheHe] mumbles: "Don't be angry. I changed my mind about joining [Root.Society.GetName]."
Oh dear... I am still proud to call you family, [new_recruit.GetFirstName].
§Y[new_recruit.GetTitledFirstName]§! will get over it.
I expected more, honestly.
§Y[new_recruit.GetTitledFirstName]§! blinks away a tear.
Weakness has no place in my blood.
You kill §Y[new_recruit.GetTitledFirstName]§! where [new_recruit.GetSheHe] sits.

My [From.GetFatherMother] tells me it does not matter which road I walk. "Sword or quill, you are my [Root.GetSonDaughter]." We spend the rest of the evening talking about other hopes and dreams of mine, and I smile whenever I think of it.
My [From.GetFatherMother] tells me [From.GetSheHe] expected more from me, then finishes [From.GetHerHis] dinner in silence.\n\nI feel awful.
Family is what matters most, after all.
I am lucky to have [From.GetHerHim].
This is not the end of my story! Nay, [From.GetSheHe] doesn't KNOW me...!
You'll show [From.GetHerHim]...!
I am an embarrassment.
My [Root.GetDuelWeapon] moves as easily as breathing now. I have learned what single combat can teach me, and perhaps it is time I turned to the other arts that [Root.Society.GetName] prizes.
I have read every campaign worth reading and fought a few worth writing about. Perhaps it is time I turned to something else.
There is no beast in these forests whose track I cannot read, and the hunt has lost its edge. Perhaps it is time I turned to something else.
I should focus on single combat.
I want to go deeper into the art of war.
I want to return to the hunt.
On second thought, I like my life as it is.

The old warriors of [Root.Society.GetName] have long wondered which road I will take. Some live for the duel in the snow, some for the war council, and some, like Ulric's own wolves, for the long hunt through the winter forests.

My brothers and sisters of [Root.Society.GetName] have long been asking when I will choose my calling. Some seek glory in the joust and the duel, others in the command of armies, and others still in the hunt, as the knights of the forest marches did in the old days.

The elders of [Root.Society.GetName] have been asking which craft of war I mean to master. Some dwarfs are known for their axe-work, some for holding a line that never breaks, and some for hunting goblins through the deeps until not one is left.
My fellow members of [Root.Society.GetName] have long been wondering when I will choose a focus for my fighting talents. Some live for the duel, others for the art of war, and others for the hunt.
I should focus on single combat.
This will lead to the §YDuelist§! trait.
I want to go deeper into the art of war.
This will lead to the §YStrategist§! trait.
I will learn the ways of the hunt.
This will lead to the §YHunter§! trait.

I have watched my warriors at their practice in the yard, and I am sure some of them grow uneasy under the constant eye of their [Root.GetTitle]. Perhaps I should admit that my own swordplay could use some guidance. If nothing else, I could join them in the snow.
I have watched the squires at their drill, and next to theirs my own blade work has grown rusty. A knight is judged in the lists. Perhaps it is time I took up the sword in earnest.
I have watched the young dwarfs at their axe-drill, and I know my own work is not what it should be. An axe that is not used grows dull, and so does the arm that swings it.

I have watched my soldiers practise their swordsmanship, and I am sure some of them are unsettled by the constant watch of their [Root.GetTitle]. Perhaps I should admit that I could use some guidance with my own blade. If nothing else, I could join their training.
I shall ask [mentor_target.GetTitledFirstName] to teach me all [mentor_target.GetSheHe] knows.
I will quietly hire a master of the blade.
I would rather do this alone.

My [From.GetRootRelation] [From.GetTitledFirstName] of [From.Society.GetName] has sent word asking for private lessons in single combat. "The [From.GetTitle] would value any guidance you can offer, my [Root.GetLordLady]," the messenger says.
I will set up [From.GetHerHis] training myself.
I will lend [From.GetHerHim] some of my best veterans to spar with.

When we started practising together, I could hardly imagine having the kind of confidence that [mentor_target.GetTitledFirstName] shows on the battlefield. But with [mentor_target.GetHerHis] training behind me, I think I have truly found my calling.

The last time we spoke, [mentor_target.GetTitledFirstName] had only praise for me. It is an odd feeling that [mentor_target.GetSheHe] is not here to see me now. I let out a sigh and clear my mind, feeling the [Root.GetDuelWeapon] in my hand. It is so natural to me now, as if part of my body.

Careful where you point that thing! a courtier cries out as I stroll back from yet another session at the training grounds, idly spinning my blade. Then, hurriedly: "Of course, a master duelist such as yourself knows best, my [Root.GetLordLady]."
I will always be grateful for your lessons, [mentor_target.GetFirstName].
A master, am I? Why, yes, I suppose I am!
It took time, but all that hard work has paid off!

My scholars have stacked old campaign books in front of me: Magnus at the gates of Kislev, the Wolf-Kings of Middenheim, the winter wars against the north. Should I not be out with the warriors instead, learning on the field?

The order's library holds the great treatises of war: the campaigns of Magnus the Pious, the Myrmidian manuals of Tilea, the old chronicles of the Emperor's wars. My scholars say every commander begins here. But surely I belong on the field, not at a desk?

The lore-keepers have brought out the Book of Battles of my hold, every engagement since the Time of Woes written down to the last cart of ale. Reading it would take years. Then again, I could simply go and watch the hold's warriors drill.

The stack of books in front of me is daunting. My scholars say these are the classics for anyone who would understand war. But surely I do not need the basics? Should I not be out in the field, watching the troops first-hand?
There is wisdom in the old campaigns.
I learn better by watching.

My commanders have come to ask my advice on the exercises they are running outside the walls of my [Root.GetCapitalHolding]. "We could use that strategic mind of yours, [Root.GetMasterMistress]," they say. Startled, I realise that my studies have paid off, and my chest swells with pride. Then I collect myself and nod: "Of course. I'd be glad to help."
Typically, what you'll want to consider in a set-up like this...
Soon you are talking and gesturing with enthusiasm, to an even mix of "Oohs" and "Aaahs".

The huntmasters of [Root.Society.GetName] say a warrior of the Wolf must follow a trail through snow and forest as the wolf does. They have offered to take me out into the Drakwald. Should I learn to read tracks, or to set snares?
The order's huntsmen have agreed to teach me, as the knights of old learned to hunt boar and beastmen in the great forests. Should I learn to follow a trail, or to lay traps?

The rangers of [Root.Society.GetName] know every tunnel and every gully, and how to hunt goblins and worse through all of them. They have offered to take me along. Should I learn to read tracks, or to set traps?
The huntsmen I have been riding with are pleased with my progress and ask what I would like to learn next. Should I learn to read tracks, or to set traps?
Tracking. I want to read the forest like a book.
Traps. Let the prey come to me.

We have been tracking for hours through the snow when I hear a sound in the brush. A thunk, a soft groan, and I know my arrow has found its mark. "Ulric's own wolves could not have done better!" one of my companions laughs. "They should call you [Root.GetFirstName] the Hunter!"

The hounds have lost the scent, but I have not. I lead the hunting party to the thicket, and there the great boar stands. One spear, well placed, and it is over. "They should call you [Root.GetFirstName] the Hunter!" one of my companions laughs. I smile.

Three days in the deeps, and the goblin raiders thought they had lost us. They had not. When the last of them falls, a ranger claps me on the shoulder. "You hunt like one of the old ones, [Root.GetFirstName]. They should call you the Hunter."

We have been tracking for hours when I hear a sound in the bushes. A thunk, followed by a soft groan, tells me that my arrow has found its mark. "They should call you [Root.GetFirstName] the Hunter!" one of my companions laughs. I smile.
I can't believe I wasn't always like this.

Ulric would be proud of you, [fellow_member.GetTitledFirstName] tells me as we stand in the snow, our breath steaming. "You have the wolf in you now. When the enemy sees you coming, they will remember the winters."

Khaine himself would smile at you, [fellow_member.GetTitledFirstName] says, wiping [fellow_member.GetHerHis] blade on a slave's tunic. "You have learned the corsair's art. Now choose what you want most from the coasts of the lesser races: their gold, their blood, or their bodies in chains."

You've the makings of a proper captain, [fellow_member.GetTitledFirstName] tells me over a cup of rum. "But a crew needs to know what its captain is after. Is it the plunder, the fight, or the slave markets of Sartosa?"
The dedication you show is admirable, [Root.GetSisterBrother], [fellow_member.GetTitledFirstName] tells me. "You have learned all we can teach."
Thank you, [fellow_member.GetFirstName]. That means a lot.
In your heart, you feel that [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] might frown upon your devotion to these people.
The plunder. Always the plunder.
The raid. Fire and steel from the sea.
Slaves. They fetch the best price.
Da old cut 'as closed up, leavin' a nice big scar. Orks don't stay 'urt. A bit o' fresh air an' a good scrap or two round [Root.Location.GetName] woz all I needed!
Da shaman said I woz done for. Da shaman woz wrong. Me guts 'ave knitted up by demselves, like dey always do. Maybe I'll krump da shaman for lyin'.
Da stump's 'ealed up proper, an' I'z used to it now. Da boyz say it makes me look 'arder. Dey'z right.
I woz smashed up so bad da boyz woz arguin' over who gets me teef. Den I woke up dis mornin', got up, an' stood up straight. "Dat's da Orky way," I tell da grot starin' at me. "Now get me some grub."
Da wound woz goin' green, an' not da good kind o' green. A painboy slapped some squig paste on it, an' now da stink's gone. Just a scar left. Lovely.
Feelin' 'arder already!
Gork's wiv me! Dat's why I don't die!
Mork's wiv me! 'E's too kunnin' ta let me croak!

Someone get me an axe! I roar. The crowd gasps as I start swinging it about, some scrambling in panic to get out of my way. One brave soul, [kinslayer_target.GetTitledFirstName], steps up to meet me. When we are done we are both laughing. "I like your rage, [Root.GetBrotherSister]!" [kinslayer_target.GetSheHe] says, wiping the sweat from [kinslayer_target.GetHerHis] brow.

Someone get me an axe! NOW! I roar at the nearest soldier. From the corner of my eye I see my [kinslayer_target.GetRootRelation] [kinslayer_target.GetTitledFirstName] watching me. As I start swinging, the rush of battle fills me, and I find myself laughing from the bottom of my belly. [kinslayer_target.GetFirstName] is laughing too, and the crowd cheers me on.

Someone get me an axe! I roar, and before anyone can answer I have torn one from the rack. The training posts do not last long. When the red mist clears, the yard is empty but for splinters, and the servants are peering at me from behind the doors.

Give me your axe! NOW! I roar at a recruit. The [Root.GetBoyGirl] obeys, and the crowd gasps as I start swinging it about, some scrambling to get out of my way. "[Root.GetFirstName], what are you doing?!" my [kinslayer_target.GetRootRelation] [kinslayer_target.GetFirstName] cries out, clutching at a blood-soaked tunic.
Aaah! I shall be the scourge of our enemies!
Aaah, by [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName]! You are a small price for my new strength!
W-whose blood is this?!
I was just... Curses, someone help us!

[From.GetTitledFirstName] went on a wild rampage through [From.GetHerHis] [From.GetCapitalHolding], and my poor [kinslayer_target.GetRootRelation] [kinslayer_target.GetTitledFirstName] was caught in it!
I will not let this insult stand!
My [kinslayer_target.GetRootRelation] should have known to stay out of the way.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has sworn vengeance on me for the death of [kinslayer_target.GetTitledFirstName]. I... don't suppose [From.GetSheHe] would accept it if I sent a courier to explain that it was an accident?
I am sure we will settle this, in time...
The Rage of a Prisoner

I can't take it any longer. "Jailer!" I shout. The one who comes to the bars is a [crossfire_target.GetManWoman] I do not know. "I heard we had a real brute down here. I got curious." I lash out at that smirk and hit the iron bar so hard my fingers crunch. My blood boils, but all I can do is crumple to the floor, the pain drowning my bloodlust.

I can't stand being caged here. In the corner of our cell, [crossfire_target.GetFirstName] stands scratching marks in the wall. "Doesn't it drive you mad?!" I growl. "YOU drive me mad!" [crossfire_target.GetSheHe] roars, flying at my throat. My blood takes hold of me, and soon the [crossfire_target.GetManWoman] is lying on the floor, whimpering, and so am I.

I have lost track of day and night, and everything reeks. The other prisoners laugh when I start attacking the wall. "Acting out your frustration?" they mock. After a few days, and some jeering from the jailer, I work an iron bar loose... The feel of a real weapon in my hand makes my blood boil.
Aaargh! Just leave me alone.
You want to go again?! I can do this all day!
Get out of my way! I am getting OUT of here!
Get out of my w- Oh, no! I'm sorry! Are you hurt?

[From.GetTitledFirstName] went on a wild rampage through the dungeons of [host_target.GetTitledFirstName]'s [host_target.GetCapitalHolding], and my poor [kinslayer_target.GetRootRelation] [kinslayer_target.GetTitledFirstName] was caught in it! The [From.GetManWoman] even made it out alive!

That [From.GetMadwomanMadman] [From.GetTitledFirstName] went on a rampage through my dungeons and escaped my [Root.GetCapitalHolding], killing [kinslayer_target.GetTitledFirstName] on the way out! Under my own roof!

That [From.GetMadwomanMadman] [From.GetTitledFirstName] went on a rampage through my dungeons and escaped my [Root.GetCapitalHolding]! As [From.GetSheHe] beat down everyone in [From.GetHerHis] path, my poor [kinslayer_target.GetRootRelation] [kinslayer_target.GetTitledFirstName] was caught in it.
Warriors from all around [target_holding.Capital.GetName] flock to my banner, and the garrison of [target_holding.GetName] is bursting with new recruits!
Word's got out dat dere's a fight comin'. Boyz from all round [target_holding.Capital.GetName] 'ave turned up wiv dere choppas, an' [target_holding.GetName] is full ta burstin'! WAAAGH!
Word comes that new warriors have stood in the yard and passed the trial. The fires of [Root.Society.GetName] burn brighter with every winter.
Word comes that new knights have passed the passage of arms and taken their vows. The ranks of [Root.Society.GetName] are growing.
The elders report that new names have been entered among [Root.Society.GetName]. The Guild grows, as it should.
Reports say that new recruits have passed our initiation, and [Root.Society.GetName] is growing in numbers!

Every seat at this table is paid for in blood, [Root.GetSocietyRank]. Mine too. [combatant_2.GetTitledFirstName] rises, armour grinding. "You want it? Then the Gods will watch us both. Only one of us walks away with their favour."
You want MY place? Mine-mine? [combatant_2.GetTitledFirstName] bares yellow teeth. "Ambitious little rat. Good. Fight-fight, then, and we see whose tail gets bitten off."
Oi! Ya wanna be a big boss like me? [combatant_2.GetTitledFirstName] cracks 'is knuckles an' grins. "Den ya gotta krump me first, [Root.GetFirstName]. Dat's da rulez."

Our table is full, [Root.GetSocietyRank]. Are you saying you want to fight me for a seat? [combatant_2.GetTitledFirstName] rises from the bench by the fire, cracking [combatant_2.GetHerHis] knuckles. "Then let the Wolf decide."

Every seat of the inner circle is taken, [Root.GetSocietyRank]. Do you mean to challenge me for mine? [combatant_2.GetTitledFirstName] rises slowly from [combatant_2.GetHerHis] chair. "Very well. A passage of arms, in the old way, before the whole order."

The council has no empty stool, [Root.GetSocietyRank]. [combatant_2.GetTitledFirstName] sets down [combatant_2.GetHerHis] tankard and looks at me for a long time. "So you want mine. Fair enough. But you'll have to take it off me, and I'm sitting on it."

Our table is already full, [Root.GetSocietyRank]. Are you saying you want to fight me for the seat? [combatant_2.GetTitledFirstName] rises from [combatant_2.GetHerHis] seat, idly cracking [combatant_2.GetHerHis] knuckles and taking a step towards me.
A duel? Yes, that is exactly what I am saying.
Oh, you misunderstand me! I did not mean to imply... I, uhm... *gulp*

Hail, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

You have proven yourself worthy of [Root.Society.GetName]. I admit defeat and step down from the seat you may now take. Use it well.

[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetTitledFirstName]

Hail, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

We mourn [combatant_2.GetTitledFirstName], but by defeating [combatant_2.GetHerHim] you have more than proven yourself worthy of the seat you sought. Use it well.

[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetTitledFirstName]
Thank you.

Hail, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

It was a valiant effort, but after the result of our duel we cannot in good conscience let you rise to the next rank of [Root.Society.GetName]. I suggest you see more battle, or spend some time on the training grounds.

[From.GetSocietyRank] [From.GetTitledFirstName]
I would be angry, if I weren't so humiliated...

Armoured warriors are waiting at my gates, their helms marked with the sign of the Gods. They served [combatant_2.GetTitledFirstName] once. "Our old lord is beaten," their spokesman says. "The Gods have chosen you over [combatant_2.GetHerHim], and so do we."

A pack of black-furred stormvermin is waiting at my burrow-gates, halberds lowered. They were [combatant_2.GetTitledFirstName]'s guard. "Old master weak-beaten," their fang-leader squeaks. "New master strong. We serve strong, yes-yes. For now."

A mob of big 'uns an' boar boyz turned up at me gates. Dey used ta be [combatant_2.GetTitledFirstName]'s ladz. "Ya krumped da old boss," da biggest one sez. "So now ya'z da boss. Where's da fightin'?"

A band of warriors in wolfskins has come to my hall. They were [combatant_2.GetTitledFirstName]'s sworn companions. "You beat our lord fairly," their eldest says. "The Wolf has spoken. We will follow you now, if you will have us."

Knights and men-at-arms in the colours of [combatant_2.GetTitledFirstName] ride into my courtyard. "Our lord yielded to you in fair combat," their captain says, bowing. "By the customs of the order, our swords are now at your service."

A troop of grim-faced dwarfs in heavy armour is standing in my hall. They were [combatant_2.GetTitledFirstName]'s hearth guard. "You beat our lord," says the eldest, "so the oath passes to you. That's the way of it. Where do we stand?"
A band of veterans who served [combatant_2.GetTitledFirstName] has come to my court. "You beat our lord," their captain says, "and we serve the strongest. We are yours, if you will have us."
Then follow me to glory.
Yes-yes. Serve well, or be eaten.
Plenty o' fightin' comin', ladz!
Then come to my fire, brothers and sisters.
I accept your service with honour.
Stand at my side, then.
Welcome to my service.
Lodge Growth Notice
The beaten Hero yields [lodge_hero_spoils.GetName] to you as the spoils of the duel.

The Dark Gods watch every battle, and every warrior of [Root.Society.GetName] knows it. Word has gone out that I march to war, and already marauders and armoured champions are gathering, each one hungry to catch the eyes of the gods on my battlefield. In a few months they will fall on my enemies like a storm out of the north.
Come, then! The gods are watching!

Blood calls to blood. The faithful of [Root.Society.GetName] have heard that I make war, and they are coming: berserkers, reavers and skull-takers, all eager to add to the Skull Throne. Khorne cares not from where the blood flows, so long as it flows. Within months they will be at my side.
Blood for the Blood God!

The Grandfather's children are patient, and generous. Through [Root.Society.GetName] I have shared the news of my war, and the rotting faithful are already shambling toward me, bloated with blessings and eager to share them with my enemies. They will come slowly, but they will come.
Let the Grandfather's gifts be shared!

All is as the Changer of Ways intended. My call has gone out through [Root.Society.GetName], and warriors and sorcerers who read their fates in the shifting stars now seek my banner. Each believes this war is one step in some greater scheme. Perhaps it is.
Come, and watch the threads unravel.

What sweeter thrill than war? I have let [Root.Society.GetName] know that I march, and the devotees of the Dark Prince are coming from every corner of my lands, hungry for the excess of battle: the scream, the clash, the ecstasy of the kill. They will be with me soon.
Come! Let us feel everything!

My war-squeak has gone out to the [Root.Society.GetName], yes-yes! Clawleaders and their clanrats now scurry through the tunnels toward me, each hoping to grab a share of the loot, and each plotting to stab the others in the back. No matter. They will die for me first, and soon.
Swarm-swarm! Kill-kill!
A new band of marauders and armoured warriors has reached me at §Y[Root.Location.GetName]§!, come to win the favour of the gods by my side.
Follow me to glory!
More of the Blood God's faithful have reached me at §Y[Root.Location.GetName]§!, roaring for skulls. They will not have to wait long for a fight.
To war!
A new column of the Grandfather's faithful has shambled into my camp at §Y[Root.Location.GetName]§!, trailing flies and a terrible stench. My enemies will fare worse than my nose.
Welcome, brothers in rot!
Warriors in shimmering mail have joined me at §Y[Root.Location.GetName]§!. Their leader says he saw this meeting in a dream, years ago.
Just as foreseen.
A new band of the Dark Prince's devotees has reached me at §Y[Root.Location.GetName]§!, painted, pierced and laughing, eager for the thrill of the next battle.
Excellent!
More clanrats have scurried out of the tunnels at §Y[Root.Location.GetName]§!, their clawleaders squeaking that they came fastest, of course, and deserve the biggest share.
Fight-fight! Or die-die!

Reinforcements from [Root.Society.GetName] have been dwindling for some weeks. The promise of the gods' favour no longer draws enough warriors to my banner. Perhaps some need another kind of persuasion...
What kind of warriors are you?!
I will share my plunder with any who join me!
I need no cowards in my army.

Fewer and fewer clanrats come out of the tunnels. The clawleaders squeak that the other warlords are hoarding their warriors, or that the slaves ran out, or that it is someone else's fault. Perhaps some need another kind of persuasion...
Cowards! I will show you how a true warlord fights!
Warpstone for every clawleader who brings more!
Bah! Let them hide in their holes.

Some of the marauders among my new warriors have begun to complain that I do not share the plunder fairly. Their chieftains demand what they call their rightful share, and threaten to take their warbands home if they do not get it.
This is but a misunderstanding...
You shall have your gold.
Begone, then! I have no need of you!

The clanrats are squeak-whining again. Their clawleaders say the loot is not shared fairly, that I keep the best for myself (which is true), and threaten to scurry back to their warrens if they are not given more.
Yes-yes, of course! You shall have more... later-soon.
Take your warpstone and be quiet!
Go! Run back to your holes!
The glory of my battles has not drawn only seasoned warriors. Many of my own people have come to [Root.Capital.GetName], eager to prove themselves before the gods against my enemies.
I will have them trained in no time!
Your zeal pleases me, but this is not your fight.
Good! You will soon meet my enemies!
Take to the longships and raid their coasts!
Word of my victories has spread through the warrens. Masses of slaves and starving clanrats have gathered at [Root.Capital.GetName], hoping to be fed, or at least to eat whoever loses.
Train them! Quick-quick!
Useless! Back to the tunnels!
To the front! Run-run!
To Clan Skryre with them! The warlocks need test subjects.

Among the warriors who answered my call today is a company unlike the rest: the Chosen, champions who have already won the favour of the Dark Gods, their armour fused to their flesh and their eyes burning. They say the gods themselves sent them to me. They will not leave when this war ends.

Today a company of the Chosen of Khorne came to my camp, their brass armour crusted with old blood and their mounts snorting fire. They have taken more skulls than they can count, and they say the Blood God sent them to take more at my side. They will not leave when this war ends.

Today a company of Blightkings came to my camp, huge and swollen beneath rusted plate, laughing as their flies settled on my warriors. The Grandfather has blessed them beyond any mortal, and they say he sent them to me. They will not leave when this war ends.

Today a company of the Chosen of Tzeentch came to my camp, their mail shifting colour as I watched and their sorcerers whispering of fates already written. They say the Architect of Fate sent them to me. They will not leave when this war ends.

Today a company of the Chosen of Slaanesh came to my camp, beautiful and terrible, their armour gleaming and their mounts as swift as the wind. They say the Dark Prince sent them to me, to taste battles finer than any they have known. They will not leave when this war ends.

Today a pack of Stormvermin came to my camp, big black-furred killers in good armour. Their warlord was stabbed in the back last week, they squeak, and now they need a new master. Me! They will not leave when this war ends... unless someone pays them more.
The gods are with me!
Mine-mine! All mine!
A company of §YChosen§! warriors joins your army for good, at half the usual upkeep.
The Chosen

[invited_warband_soldier.GetFirstName], a champion of [Root.Society.GetName], has come to my hall. [invited_warband_soldier.GetSheHeCap] says the Dark Gods have shown [invited_warband_soldier.GetHerHim] that glory waits at my side, and asks only to lead my warriors against my enemies.

[invited_warband_soldier.GetFirstName], a champion of the Blood God, has come to my hall with a string of skulls at [invited_warband_soldier.GetHerHis] belt. [invited_warband_soldier.GetSheHeCap] asks only to lead my warriors where the blood runs thickest.

[invited_warband_soldier.GetFirstName], a bloated champion of Grandfather Nurgle, has shambled into my hall, cheerfully scratching at [invited_warband_soldier.GetHerHis] sores. [invited_warband_soldier.GetSheHeCap] offers to lead my warriors and share the Grandfather's gifts with my enemies.

[invited_warband_soldier.GetFirstName], a champion of the Changer of Ways, has come to my hall on the very day [invited_warband_soldier.GetSheHe] wrote that [invited_warband_soldier.GetSheHe] would. [invited_warband_soldier.GetSheHeCap] says it is fated that [invited_warband_soldier.GetSheHe] lead my armies, and that [invited_warband_soldier.GetSheHe] has already seen how my enemies will fall.

[invited_warband_soldier.GetFirstName], a champion of the Dark Prince, has swept into my hall in perfumed armour. [invited_warband_soldier.GetSheHeCap] craves the thrill of command, and offers to lead my warriors to battles worth savouring.

[invited_warband_soldier.GetFirstName], a scarred clawleader of the [Root.Society.GetName], has scurried into my warren, bowing low and squeaking of [invited_warband_soldier.GetHerHis] many victories (some of them probably true). [invited_warband_soldier.GetSheHeCap] wants to lead my clanrats, yes-yes, and promises to be loyal-loyal.

[invited_warband_soldier.GetFirstName], a big, mean boss of [Root.Society.GetName], has stomped into my camp and flattened two of my guards to make a point. 'Oi! I'z da best fighta round 'ere. Let me lead ya boyz an' we'll krump 'em all!'
The weakest of my commanders will make way for you.
Lead my warriors well, [invited_warband_soldier.GetFirstName].
Welcome, champion. Your chance will come.
Yes-yes! The weakest one will be... removed.
Lead my clanrats, and do not fail me.
Stay, stay. I may need you later-soon.
Oi, you! Yer sacked. 'E's da boss now.
Right. You'z a boss now.
Stick around. Might need ya.
My call has gone out to [Root.Society.GetName], and the war-horns of the north have answered. Which of the champions' followers should march for me?
I have called on [Root.Society.GetName], and the Blood God's faithful are howling for war. Which of them should I unleash?
I have called on [Root.Society.GetName], and the Grandfather's children are rising from their sickbeds to march. Which of them should come?
I have called on [Root.Society.GetName], and the Architect of Fate has already arranged for warriors to be waiting. Which of them should I take?
I have called on [Root.Society.GetName], and the Dark Prince's devotees are wild with excitement at the thought of war. Which of them should come?
I have squeaked my summons to the [Root.Society.GetName], and the warrens are churning. Clawpacks, weapon teams and slaves are ready to swarm out of the tunnels. Which should I send?
I've bellowed for [Root.Society.GetName], an' every boy in squigs' reach wants in on da fight. Which lot should come?
Chaos Warriors and their marauders!
The marauder horsemen!
The marauder hordes!
On second thought, I do not need them yet.
Stormvermin and clanrats!
The weapon teams! Ratling guns and jezzails!
The slaves! All of them!
No-no, not yet. Later-later.
Da Boyz! Big an' 'ard!
Da wolf riders! Fast as anyfing!
Da gobbo mob! Loadsa gobbos!
Nah, not yet.
Summoned Warband
Warband Summoned
This ruler has called the warband to war, and cannot call again until there is peace.
Summon the Warband
Call on your warband to send a great host to your capital for this war. The host leaves when the war ends, and you cannot call again until you are at peace.
A great host of your warband gathers at your capital for this war.

Da ladz of [Root.Society.GetName] keep askin' who I'm gonna krump. Some bosses like a big fight out in da open where everyone can see 'em. Some go up inta da mountains ta bash stunties. Some hide in da trees an' jump out on gits. A boss needs ta pick, or da ladz'll pick a new boss.

After much fight-kill with fellow clanrats, it is time I learned to kill-kill in a special way. Yes-yes. A wise Warlord knows where his strength lies. In the tunnels, where the man-things cannot follow? Among the Stormvermin, at the head of the black-furred elite? Or in leading from behind, as all truly great Warlords do?
Out in da open! Where everyone can see me krump 'em!
Up da mountains! Dem stuntie gits need bashin'!
Inta da caves! We'z sneakin' up on da stunties in da dark!
Inta da trees. We'z gonna ambush 'em proppa sneaky.
The tunnels! Down-down, where none can follow!
The Stormvermin! Black fur, sharp blades!
Leading! From the back, safe-safe, as is proper!
Nah. Not yet.
Not now. Later-later, perhaps.
My promotion was celebrated with much squeaking and only a little stabbing. Afterwards, creeping past the clan's armour-pile, I noticed that no one was looking. No one at all...
Mine-mine! HANDS OFF!

My [Root.GetDuelWeapon] has drunk deep in the pits, and there is no one left among my followers who will face me. Perhaps the Gods would rather see me walk another of the paths of [Root.Society.GetName].
I have broken enough armies to know how it is done. Every siege and every charge is the same lesson told again. Perhaps it is time I walked another of the paths of [Root.Society.GetName].
I have lost count of the bodies I have opened in my dungeon, and the screams no longer surprise me. Perhaps the Gods would rather see me walk another of the paths of [Root.Society.GetName].
The duel. Let my blade speak for me.
The art of conquest. I will learn to break whole armies.
Back to the dungeon. My playthings are waiting.
On second thought, my path suits me well.

The warriors of [Root.Society.GetName] are watching me, waiting to see which path I will walk to glory. Some live for the duel, blade against blade before the eyes of the Gods. Some study the slaughter of armies, and win their wars before the first charge. And some find their worship in the dungeon, where every scream is a prayer.
The duel. Let my blade speak for me.
This will lead to the §YDuelist§! trait.\n
The art of conquest. I will learn to break whole armies.
This will lead to the §YStrategist§! trait.\n
The dungeon. The Gods hear screams best of all.
This will lead to the §YTorturer§! trait.\n
I will choose another time.

I have watched my warriors fight in the pits, and I have seen some of them sneer when they think I am not looking. A champion who cannot best their own followers will not stay a champion for long. I could seek out a better blade than mine to learn from. Or I could simply fight until I am the best.
[mentor_target.GetTitledFirstName] will teach me everything [mentor_target.GetSheHe] knows.
I will pay a pit-fighter to beat the clumsiness out of me.
I need no teacher. Only enemies.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has sent word, asking me to teach [From.GetHerHim] the ways of the blade. 'The Gods favour those who raise up worthy champions,' the messenger says, keeping his eyes on the floor.
I will train [From.GetHerHim] myself. In blood, if need be.
I will send [From.GetHerHim] some of my best killers to spar with.

When I began training with [mentor_target.GetTitledFirstName], I could barely follow [mentor_target.GetHerHis] strikes. Today I cut [mentor_target.GetHerHim] on the third pass. [mentor_target.GetSheHeCap] laughed, spat blood and called me a true champion of the Gods.

[mentor_target.GetTitledFirstName] is gone, and [mentor_target.GetHerHis] skull may already sit on some altar. [mentor_target.GetSheHeCap] would have liked to see this. My [Root.GetDuelWeapon] moves as if it were part of my arm, and no one in the pits will face me any more.

Today a warrior who used to sneer at me drew steel in the pits. He did not finish the sentence he began. The rest of my followers have stopped sneering. They call me a master of the blade now, and they mean it.
I will not forget your lessons, [mentor_target.GetFirstName].
A master? Yes. Yes, I suppose I am.
Blood and practice. Nothing more was needed.

My sorcerers and chieftains have heaped the plunder of a dozen libraries before me: maps of the southern kingdoms, the treatises of Tilean generals, the scratched battle-plans of dead warlords. 'Know your prey,' the old ones say. But is a champion of Chaos meant to read? Should I not be out among the warriors, watching them fight?
The southlings' own books will teach me how to break them.
I will learn by watching the warband fight.

My chieftains came to me today for advice on how to take the walls of a southern town. I spoke for an hour. When I finished, the oldest of them had the look of a man who has seen something holy. 'The Gods have given you the eye of a conqueror,' he said.
Listen well. This is how we will break them...
Soon you are drawing in the dirt with your dagger, and the chieftains crowd closer to see.\n

The old torturer who has shared my dungeon these past months is pleased with me. My hands are steady, my patience is endless, and I have learned to make a scream last until dawn. He asks what I would like to learn next. The Gods whisper many suggestions.
Their faces. Teach me what else I can do to their faces.
I want to see how far pain and pleasure can be blurred.

Tonight my latest guest begged the Gods to take him. They did not, of course. They were watching me. When I finally climbed out of the dungeon, my servants would not meet my eyes, and I heard one of them whisper a new name for me in the dark.
Let them whisper. Let them fear.

Power rushes into me like a storm. The Ruinous Powers have weighed my sacrifices and found them worthy. All the slaughter, all the offerings, all the years of devotion have been repaid. I am a Champion of Chaos Undivided, and the Gods will be watching what I do next.

The rot flows through me, warm and welcome as a fever. Grandfather Nurgle has seen my devotion and rewarded it with his blessings. I am a Champion of Nurgle, and my body will never again be entirely my own.

Power crackles through me, shifting colour with every heartbeat. The Changer of Ways has rewarded my schemes, as he always meant to. I am a Champion of Tzeentch, and every path before me is now part of his plan.

Ecstasy floods through me, so sharp it is almost pain. The Dark Prince has rewarded my excesses with more than I could ever have asked for. I am a Champion of Slaanesh, and nothing will ever be enough again.
Rage pours through me like molten iron. The Blood God has counted the skulls I have taken and found the tally good. I am a Champion of Khorne, and the Skull Throne will have more.
For the Ruinous Powers!
Grandfather's blessings upon us all!
All is as he has foreseen.
More. Always more.
Blood for the Blood God! Skulls for the Skull Throne!

My rituals and sacrifices have not gone unnoticed. Something small has crawled out of the smoke of my last offering, shapeless and hungry. Imps are the least of the least, minor daemons born of loosed emotions, cycling endlessly through shapes that echo the thoughts that birthed them. Only when a Dark God claims an Imp does it become something.\n\nWhich of the Dark Gods shall claim mine?
§GNurgle§!
§BTzeentch§!
§PSlaanesh§!
§RKhorne§!

The Imp swells into a tiny Nurgling, delicate, foul and green. It looks like a small withered pea dimpled with sphincters that leak a yellow wetness, and it giggles whenever someone near it falls sick. It has named itself Bubo.
Welcome, little Bubo.

The Imp becomes a small ball of pink flesh, like a tiny Horror of Tzeentch. It sits and quivers, spitting blue and pink flames from its many mouths, and scorches the floor wherever it drags itself. Where it goes, thoughts of rebellion follow. It is a Fearling.
Welcome, little Fearling.

The Imp takes the form of a beautiful young woman no taller than a child, with scintillating hair and a smile that steals the breath. It whispers to the men of my court, draining their senses and urging them always further towards the glory they seek. It is a Muse.
Welcome, little Muse.

The Imp hardens into a miniature warrior in black armour, a tiny Chaos Warrior with the temper of the most vicious champion of Khorne. It feeds on rage and hate, and stirs both in everyone it meets. It is a Malice.
Welcome, little Malice.

Through endless training and endless slaughter, my mind and body have learned to sink into a rage that never ends. I no longer feel my wounds. I thirst only for blood. I have become a Berserker of Khorne.
BLOOD FOR THE BLOOD GOD!
New warriors have bled at our initiation rites, and [Root.Society.GetName] grows stronger. The Gods will be pleased.
More clanrats have joined [Root.Society.GetName]. More claws, more blades, more fodder. Good-good.
More boyz 'ave turned up wantin' ta join [Root.Society.GetName]. Da more da better, 'cos dat means more ta krump wiv.

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName], who walks the same bloody road,

[waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName] has dared to march on my lands. The Dark Gods watch every warband that answers a call to war, and they watch the ones who stay at home too. Bring your warriors. There will be skulls enough for both of us, and I will make sure [Root.Society.GetName] hears whose blade took the most.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName], most-cunning ally-friend,

The fool-thing [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName] attacks my burrows! Yes-yes, attacks ME! Come quick-quick with your claws and we will gnaw them together. The other Warlords will hear how bravely you fought at my side (or behind me, it is the same). Refuse and... I will remember. Skaven always remember.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledName]

Oi, [Root.GetFirstName]!

Dat git [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName] finks he can krump me. He's wrong. Bring yer boyz an' we'll give 'im a proper stompin'. Dere's loot in it, an' a good scrap, an' I'll tell all da ladz who smashed da most 'eads. Don't make me come over dere an' ask twice.

[waraid_ally.GetFirstName], da Boss

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName], [Root.GetSisterBrother] of the Wolf,

[waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName] has come against me with fire and steel. Ulric despises those who sit by the hearth while their kin bleed in the snow. Ride to me with your warriors and we shall fight as the pack fights, shoulder to shoulder. When the war is done, every Warrior of Ulric from Middenheim to the Drakwald will know your name.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledName]

To the honourable [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

[waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName] has broken the peace and marched against my lands. I call upon you, as one knight to another, to honour the oaths of our brotherhood and ride to my aid. Your deeds on the field shall be told in every chapter house of the Knightly Orders. This I swear upon my sword.

In hope of your lance,
[waraid_ally.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName], of the Warriors Guild,

[waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName] has marched on my hold. I have written the name in the book of grudges and I mean to strike it out in blood. Bring your axes. A dawi who helps settle another's grudge is not forgotten. The Guild will hear of it, and so will the ancestors.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

[waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName] has attacked my lands. A warrior's blood is not made for idleness, so I ask you to join me against my enemies. Fight well, and I will see that [Root.Society.GetName] hears of it.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledName]
Blood and glory! I march.
Yes-yes, I come. Quick-quick!
'Ere we go! 'Ere we go!
The pack rides together!
For honour! I ride to your side.
My axe is yours. Let the grudge be settled.
I gladly accept. May my weapon taste the blood of your enemies!
I have my own skulls to take.
Too busy-busy. Another time, yes?
Nah. Got me own scrap ta sort out.
Not this time. My own hearth needs me.
Other duties keep me from the field.
My own hold needs my axe.
I have other matters to attend to.

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName], who walks the same bloody road,

I march on [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName], and the Dark Gods have promised me the walls will fall. Join the warpath. Share the slaughter, share the plunder, and share the glory when I tell [Root.Society.GetName] who stood beside me before the gates.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName], most-trusted (for now) ally,

I go to take the lands of [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName]. Easy-easy conquest, yes, but more claws make it quicker. Join me and we split the spoils, fair-fair, I promise. The other Warlords will hear of your great help. Very great. Almost as great as mine.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledName]

Oi, [Root.GetFirstName]!

I'm goin' ta krump [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName]. Gonna be a proper WAAAGH! Well, a little one. Come along wiv yer boyz. Dere's plenty of 'eads ta smash an' stuff ta grab, an' if we win I'll tell everyone ya was nearly as 'ard as me.

[waraid_ally.GetFirstName], da Boss

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName], [Root.GetSisterBrother] of the Wolf,

I ride against [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName], and the pack hunts best together. Join me. Ulric gives his favour to the bold, and if the hunt ends well the Warriors of Ulric will hear of your courage from my own mouth.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledName]

To the honourable [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

I have just cause against [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName], and I go to press it with the lance. Ride with me. Should Fortune grant us victory, the Knightly Orders shall hear of your valour from my own lips.

In hope of your lance,
[waraid_ally.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName], of the Warriors Guild,

I march on [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName] to settle a grudge older than both of us. Bring your axes. If we win, the Guild will hear that you stood with me, and the book will have one line fewer in it.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

I am going to war against [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName], and I would have you at my side. Join me, and if we win I will see that [Root.Society.GetName] hears of your part in it.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

I hear [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName] begged for your sword, and you refused. Wise. The weak deserve no allies. Join me instead and we will feast on the carcass together. The Gods favour those who choose the winning side.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

The fool-thing [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName] begged you for help and you said no-no. Clever! Very clever. Now help ME instead, and we will share-share the spoils. Of course we will.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledName]

Oi!

I 'eard [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName] asked ya for help an' ya told 'im ta get stuffed. Ha! Dat's da spirit. Now come an' help ME krump 'im instead. Even more fun.

[waraid_ally.GetFirstName], da Boss

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

Word reached me that [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName] called on you and you would not ride. Good. A wolf knows which way the wind blows. Ride with me instead, and we will share the hunt and its glory.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledName]

To the honourable [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

I am told [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName] sought your aid and was refused. A sound judgement. My cause is the just one, and my offer is as good as any. Ride with me, and you shall have my thanks, and more besides should victory be ours.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

I hear [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName] asked for your axe and you kept it. Good. It would have been a shame to write your name in the book next to theirs. Bring it to me instead.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

I heard that you turned down [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName]. My offer is a better one. Join me against [waraid_enemy.GetHerHim], and if we win I will see that [Root.Society.GetName] hears of your part in it.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledName]

A rider brings a letter from [waraid_ally.GetTitledFirstName]. The war against [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName] is over, and we have won it.\n\n[waraid_ally.GetSheHeCap] writes that the tale of my deeds is already being told among [Root.Society.GetName], and that it grows with every telling.

A letter from [waraid_ally.GetTitledFirstName]. The war with [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName] has ended in a white peace. Our enemy came for [waraid_ally.GetHerHis] lands and went home with nothing.\n\n[waraid_ally.GetSheHeCap] thanks me for standing with [waraid_ally.GetHerHim] and promises to speak well of me among [Root.Society.GetName].

A letter from [waraid_ally.GetTitledFirstName]. The war against [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName] has ended in a white peace, and we have nothing to show for it but our dead.\n\n[waraid_ally.GetSheHeCap] does not blame me outright. But [waraid_ally.GetSheHe] does not thank me either, and I doubt [Root.Society.GetName] will hear my name from [waraid_ally.GetHerHis] lips.

A letter from [waraid_ally.GetTitledFirstName], and it is not a kind one. The war against [waraid_enemy.GetTitledFirstName] is lost.\n\n[waraid_ally.GetSheHeCap] writes that I fought like a peasant with a pitchfork, and that [Root.Society.GetName] will hear exactly how little I did.
Victory! Let them tell the tale.
Is that all? I expected a share of the spoils.
We held. That is enough.
The nerve of this brazen fool!
What should I have done differently?
There is truth in these harsh words. I must abandon my craven ways.

Another letter from [waraid_ally.GetTitledFirstName]. The skulls of our enemies are piled before [waraid_ally.GetHerHis] altar, and [waraid_ally.GetSheHe] invites me to the victory feast. There will be blood-wine and offerings, and champions fighting in the pit to show the Gods who is worthiest. A guest who does not fight is not a guest for long.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledFirstName] invites me to a victory feast in [waraid_ally.GetHerHis] burrows. There will be warpstone-cured meat, gnawed bones and long speeches about how [waraid_ally.GetSheHe] won the war alone. There will also, very probably, be poison. One does not refuse a Warlord's feast. One also does not eat first.

[waraid_ally.GetFirstName] wants ta celebrate. Dat means a feast, an' dat means a fight, 'cos dere's no proper feast wivout one. Da ladz will all be watchin' ta see if I'm 'ard enough ta stand wiv 'im.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledFirstName] invites me to a great hunt in the forests of [waraid_ally.Capital.GetName]. The Wolf God's warriors celebrate as the pack does, with a chase through the snow and a kill shared at the fire. A great boar has been seen in the woods, and whoever brings it down will be honoured above all.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledFirstName] is holding a tourney to celebrate our victory, and I am invited to ride in the lists. The Knightly Orders will be watching, and so will half the realm. A good showing will be talked of for years. A bad one will be talked of for longer.

[waraid_ally.GetTitledFirstName] has opened the best kegs in [waraid_ally.GetHerHis] hold to toast our victory, and I am invited to drink with [waraid_ally.GetHerHim] and see the grudge struck from the book. The dawi drink to their victories as seriously as they fight for them. Leaving the table early would shame my beard.

Another letter from [waraid_ally.GetTitledFirstName]. [waraid_ally.GetSheHeCap] invites me to celebrate our victory with feasting and contests of arms, and to show [waraid_ally.GetHerHis] court the warrior [waraid_ally.GetSheHe] has been boasting about.
To the pit! Let the Gods see me fight.
I come. But I bring my own food.
Time for a proper scrap!
To the hunt!
I shall ride in the lists.
Bring out the kegs!
I happily accept!
Decline the invitation. It is not to my taste.
I win the contest, and the respect of my host.
I come off worst.

Another letter from [waraid_ally.GetTitledFirstName]. Since the celebration [waraid_ally.GetSheHe] has written often, about old battles and new enemies, and lately about less warlike things. Surely there is a reason for all this letter-writing?
Our time together is a memory I will always cherish.
I never thought I would find love through war...
My letters to [waraid_ally.GetFirstName] are nothing but formality.

They came at dusk, a band of armoured warriors with the marks of the Dark Gods burned into their shields. Their leader threw a token from [waraid_ally.GetTitledFirstName] at my feet. 'Our lord says you fought well,' he said. 'We fight for you now.' They have not asked for pay. They have asked for enemies.

A pack of clanrats crept into my burrows tonight, led by a scarred Stormvermin with a message from [waraid_ally.GetTitledFirstName]. A gift, it said. Loyal warriors, it said. They are probably spies. They are certainly warriors, though, and spies who fight are still warriors.

A mob of boyz turned up at da gate, shovin' an' laughin', wiv a message from [waraid_ally.GetFirstName]: 'Dese ladz fink you'z a proper Boss. Keep 'em.' They have already eaten two goats and started a fight with my guards. They will do nicely.

A company of hard-eyed warriors in wolfskins rode in from the north today, sent by [waraid_ally.GetTitledFirstName]. They fought beside me in the last war and have asked to stay. 'The pack goes where the hunt is,' their sergeant said, and that was the end of the matter.

A company of men-at-arms and a handful of knights arrived today under the banner of [waraid_ally.GetTitledFirstName]. They bear a letter: in thanks for my valour, they are to serve me for as long as I have need of them. Their armour is battered and their lances well used. They are exactly what I need.

A column of dawi veterans marched up to my gate today, beards braided for war, carrying a sealed message from [waraid_ally.GetTitledFirstName]. They are to serve me, it says, until the debt of the last war is paid in full. Knowing the dawi, that may take a very long time.
A company of veterans arrived today, sent by [waraid_ally.GetTitledFirstName] in thanks for my part in the war. They have fought beside me once already, and they have asked to serve me for good.
They are welcome in my host.
Brother in Arms
